URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/7/19/andy-burnhams-in-tray-the-challenges-facing-the-new-uk-pm
(WebFetch — Al Jazeera, 19 July 2026)

Fiscal situation:
- Government spent £110bn ($148bn) on debt interest in 2025-26, about 8% of all public spending.
- Taxes are forecast to reach their highest share of the economy since World War II by decade's end.
- Borrowing has run higher than planned in 2026.

Anand Menon (director, UK in a Changing Europe):
- "Burnham has relatively little fiscal room for manoeuvre." New spending must be raised through
  taxation rather than borrowing.
- On living standards: "people don't just want to listen to what you're saying, they want to see
  changes for the better."
- On the anti-Reform coalition: "almost 70 percent are willing to do whatever it takes to stop
  them being elected."

Economy: the incoming PM inherits an economy that has barely grown in two decades.

Reform UK polling: Labour entered government in 2024 with 33% of the vote vs Reform's 14%; recent
polls show Reform at 24-26% with Labour close behind.

North Sea: Burnham expected to allow new North Sea oil and gas drilling.
